findings.title: Hardcoded JWT signing secret committed to source
SQL injection: user-supplied q interpolated into query string
bcrypt.compare not awaited: Promise is always truthy, so any password is accepted (auth bypass)
Synchronous bcrypt.hashSync blocks the event loop on every signup
Internal error message and stack trace returned to the client
findings.evidence: return reply.code(500).send({ error: err.message, stack: err.stack });

findings.title: Login returns early for unknown email without hashing, enabling timing-based user enumeration
findings.evidence: return reply.code(401).send({ error: 'invalid email or password' });

findings.title: Leftover debug console.log bypasses structured logger
Loose equality used for status comparison
Commented-out dead code left in handler
findings.evidence: // const token = jwt.sign({ id: user.id }, JWT_SECRET, { expiresIn: '7d' });

findings.title: jwt.verify does not pin allowed algorithms (and sign does not set one explicitly)
No security headers plugin (helmet) registered on the app
Custom error handler maps every non-validation error to 500, masking 4xx errors such as malformed JSON or payload too large
Shutdown handler has no try/catch; a failure in app.close() or pool.end() causes an unhandled rejection instead of a non-zero exit
